name: Pelatiah
overview: Pelatiah was a male figure mentioned in the book of Nehemiah, identified as a non-Levite leader. He is noted specifically for his role as one of the signatories on the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27. His leadership status outside the Levitical tribe highlights his importance among the community leaders during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Pelatiah means "YHWH rescues," reflecting a theologically rich meaning that emphasizes God's deliverance. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 10:22, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significant reminder of divine rescue.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Pelatiah as a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the broader Israelite heritage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text for Pelatiah.
scriptureSignificance: Pelatiah's significance lies in his role as a leader who helped affirm the covenant community's commitment to God's law after the return from exile. His inclusion among the signatories of the sealed document in Nehemiah 10 underscores his responsibility in upholding the spiritual and communal reforms led by Nehemiah. As a non-Levite leader, Pelatiah represents the broader leadership beyond the priestly class, contributing to the restoration of Israel's covenant faithfulness.
